correctness.rationale: For d>=3 and t in (0,1], symmetry and uniqueness force a centered ellipsoid with axial and common transverse radii. John containment is equivalent to A<=t, A^2+(d-1)B^2<=1, and maximizing A B^(d-1) yields transition t_J=1/sqrt(d). The clipped cross-polytope vertex list yields Löwner inequalities V>=1 and t^2/U^2+(1-t)^2/V^2<=1; strictly concave log precision optimization yields transition t_L=1-sqrt((d-1)/d). Exact positive isotropic contact measures check optimality; derivative of log volume ratio is controlled by a strictly increasing H_d with one interior zero, and asymptotic t_d~(2d)^-1/2 gives (2ed)^-1/4 relative improvement. Independently evaluated numerical convex optima in d=3,6,10 with root residuals at numerical tolerance. The proof establishes all dimensions, not the samples.
